The Medicaid Application-Ready Checklist

Dad's records to find, keep and ask about, in case your family ever applies.

Download PDF

Dad is managing fine and nobody is applying for anything. You don't need to know any rules to start on this list: it names the records worth finding, a few worth keeping as you go, and the questions worth writing down for later. Go through it with Dad's say-so and check what you've done. Anything unchecked is something to get to when it suits you both, not a verdict about Dad or about you.

Find

Keep

Ask about

What this checklist doesn't do

It helps you find, keep and ask. It doesn't say which records Dad's state requires or how far back they need to go, what any record means for Medicaid, or whether or when anyone should apply. Rules vary by state, so those questions go to your Medicaid planner or the appropriate licensed professional. Nothing here is legal, financial or tax advice.

Ready for the next step?

You've seen which of Dad's records to find and keep, and your questions for later are written down. The planning interview asks about your family's situation and gives you a free planning report you can bring to any conversation about paying for care.

Where this comes from

Items marked 1 follow the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau's list of financial documents to keep organized and available. Items marked 2 follow the National Institute on Aging's checklist. The rest come from the Medicaid Planning Roadmap's own working list for this step.
